name: Community meal share
description: Households in one building split the parts of a shared meal so everyone eats well with less effort.

stages.label: Get to know you
stages.description: A short chat about what your household loves, avoids and can cook.

stages.label: What we share
stages.description: Shared tastes, hard constraints, schedule overlaps and skill pairings.

stages.label: Agree a rotation
stages.description: Two or three rotation options. Everyone says support, can live with it, or object.

stages.label: Cook and eat
stages.description: Claim a part of each meal. Everything lands in your own calendar.

stages.label: Keep it going
stages.description: Reminders, quick feedback after each meal, and small adjustments.

stages.label: Connections
stages.description: Suggested pairings, such as two households who want to learn the same dish.

intake.intro: Hi! I'm helping your building set up a shared meal. Everyone brings one part to the rooftop dining room and we eat together. I'll ask a few quick questions about your household, and you'll see and approve exactly how I summarise you before anyone else does. You can type or use your phone's dictation, and stop and come back any time.

topics.question: Who's in your household, and how many people would be eating (adults and kids)?
What cuisines or dishes does your household love?
Are there foods you'd rather avoid, even if they're not a strict requirement?
Any dietary requirements the meal must respect, such as vegetarian, halal, or no pork?
Any food allergies? These stay private: I only ever show them as a constraint like "no nuts in this meal", never linked to your household.
How confident do you feel cooking for a group, and which parts of a meal do you most enjoy making?
Which weeknights could you usually make a shared dinner?
Last one: is there anything you'd love to learn to cook, or to learn from a neighbour?

profileFields.label: People eating
profileFields.description: Number of people in the household who would eat at shared meals.

profileFields.label: About the household
profileFields.description: Who is in the household, in their own words (for example: two adults, kids aged 4 and 7).

profileFields.label: Cuisines loved
profileFields.description: Cuisines or dishes the household loves.

profileFields.label: Foods avoided
profileFields.description: Foods the household would rather avoid (preferences, not strict requirements).

profileFields.label: Dietary requirements
profileFields.description: Requirements every meal must respect, such as vegetarian, halal, no pork.

profileFields.label: Allergies
profileFields.description: Food allergies. Only surfaced as anonymous constraints on every meal.

profileFields.label: Cooking confidence
profileFields.description: How confident the household feels cooking for a group.

profileFields.label: Parts they enjoy making
profileFields.description: Which parts of a meal the household enjoys making. A meal can be split by course (main, side, dessert) or by component (protein, carb, veg).

profileFields.label: Free weeknights
profileFields.description: Weeknights the household could usually make a shared dinner.

profileFields.label: Would love to learn
profileFields.description: Dishes or skills the household would love to learn, possibly from a neighbour.

outputs.label: Shared tastes
outputs.description: Cuisines, dishes or preferences several households share.

outputs.label: Hard constraints
outputs.description: Requirements every meal must respect. Never attributed to a household.

outputs.label: Tensions
outputs.description: Real trade-offs, such as a popular cuisine that conflicts with another household's avoidances.

outputs.label: Schedule overlaps
outputs.description: Nights that suit the most households.

outputs.label: Skill pairings
outputs.description: Unexpected pairings: someone who wants to learn what another loves to cook.

outputs.label: Minority views
outputs.description: Something only one or two households raised, kept visible rather than averaged away.

proposal.label: Rotation plan
proposal.guidance: Start monthly or fortnightly. Everyone brings their part to the shared rooftop dining room and eats together. Aim for a meal that is as complete and accessible as possible for a busy family with young kids: a main, sides, and something kids will eat. A meal can be split by course (main, side, dessert) or by component (protein, carb, veg); pick whichever fits the number of households.
